Server side should ensure that subsequent repeated requests with the same idempotency key is ignored or that its effect is idempotent - that doing the action twice or more is the same as doing it just once. - Other metadata: a RESTful API endpoint could allow the client to add its own metadata object in the request, with arbitrary json data allowed as long as its top level is an object. - Controller resource: A common question in REST is how can complex transaction be modelled if REST is mostly like plain CRUD on data. Answer: Principal rotations are rotations around the three axes of a coordinate system: the x, y, and z axes. Any rotation in three-dimensional space can be decomposed into a combination of these principal rotations. To perform a rotation around a point or axis in three-dimensional space, you can first rotate around the x axis, then rotate around the y axis, and finally rotate around the z axis. This is known as the ""axis-angle"" representation of a rotation. In two dimensions, the principal rotations are around the x and y axes, and a rotation can be decomposed into a combination of these two. Principal rotations form a group under the operation of composition, meaning that if you perform one rotation followed by another, the result is also a rotation.
